title: 2018 AMC 12B 16
statement: The solutions to the equation \((z+6)^8=81\) are connected in the complex plane to form a convex regular polygon, three of whose vertices are labeled \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C.\) What is the least possible area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

solutions.text:
Translating by \(6,\) the solutions of \(z^8=81\) are eight points on a circle of radius \(81^{\frac{1}{8}}=\sqrt3,\) forming a regular octagon. The minimum-area triangle uses three consecutive vertices.

Take \(A=\left(\tfrac12\sqrt6,\tfrac12\sqrt6\right),\) \(B=(\sqrt3,0),\) and \(C=\left(\tfrac12\sqrt6,-\tfrac12\sqrt6\right).\) Then \(AC=\sqrt6\) and the height is \(\sqrt3-\tfrac12\sqrt6,\) so the area is \[ \begin{gathered} \tfrac12\cdot\sqrt6\left(\sqrt3-\tfrac12\sqrt6\right) \\ =\tfrac{3}{2}\sqrt2-\tfrac{3}{2}. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Shifting by \(6\) does not change the shape; the roots of \(z^8=81\) form a regular octagon
The circumradius is \(81^{\frac{1}{8}}=\sqrt3,\) and the smallest triangle uses three consecutive vertices
